findings.title: Deleting cache leaves the UI showing the old cache status
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. That query is what supplies cacheUpdatedAt, and SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads it with refetchOnWindowFocus: false. After a successful delete the menu still shows the previous "Last updated" time and "Delete cached data" until a full remount, so the action looks like it failed.

findings.title: Cache status treats expired rows as a live cache
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and takes max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. getCachedAvailability only treats a row as a hit when expiresAt is still in the future. Any leftover expired row therefore makes connected calendars report cacheUpdatedAt and the dropdown offers "Delete cached data" even though availability lookups are already cache misses. The status does not mean the cache is serving data.

findings.title: Backfill stamps every existing cache as updated at migrate time
findings.body: The new updatedAt column is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration timestamp rather than when it was actually written. CalendarCache has no createdAt; the only freshness signal already stored is expiresAt (writes set it to about now + 30 days). After deploy, every Google credential with any historical cache row shows "Last updated" as the deploy time, including stale and expired caches, which defeats the status feature. Backfill from expiresAt minus the cache TTL (and drop the default only if you still want Prisma @updatedAt to own later writes) before this ships; it cannot be reconstructed later.

findings.title: Cache delete is undone by active Google watches
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler only runs calendarCache.deleteMany for the credential. It does not stop google channel subscriptions on SelectedCalendar, and GoogleCalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache (called from the webhook path) writes CalendarCache again and then touches those selected calendars. The confirmation copy says the delete cannot be undone, but the next notification recreates the rows. Users clearing a bad cache will see it return with no explanation, and a reload can show a new timestamp as if the delete did not stick.

findings.title: Delegation calendar cache is invisible to status and delete
findings.body: Cache status is loaded only via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(connected calendar credential ids). The same repository documents that in-memory delegation credentials use negative ids that are not stored on CalendarCache, and reads for those users are keyed by userId plus the free/busy key so they can reuse a real credential's cache. Those org/delegation Google connections — the users the calendar-cache feature flag is aimed at — always get cacheUpdatedAt null, so the new menu never offers delete. deleteCacheHandler cannot fix that either: it requires a Credential row with id = credentialId and userId = the session user, which does not match a negative in-memory id or a cache row owned by another credential id.

findings.title: dev:cron now calls tsx, which this package does not depend on
findings.body: dev:cron changed from ts-node cron-tester.ts to npx tsx cron-tester.ts. ts-node is a declared devDependency; tsx is not in this package.json, and the app pins Yarn 3.4.1, where npx is not the workspace runner and will try to fetch tsx outside the lockfile. yarn dev:cron fails offline or in CI, or runs an unpinned tsx. This change is unrelated to calendar cache and should stay on the declared runner or add tsx as a dependency and invoke it through Yarn.

findings.title: Webhook helper is macOS-only and writes .env relative to the cwd
findings.body: The new script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '' (BSD sed). On GNU sed that form treats '' as the script and does not edit the file, so Linux developers never get the tunnel URL written. ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the current working directory, not the script path: running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root writes the parent directory's .env, not the app env file. cleanup also always exits 0, so a failed tunnel startup is reported as success.

findings.title: No tests for deleteCache ownership or status mapping
findings.body: deleteCache is a new authenticated mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a client-supplied credentialId after a userId check, and connectedCalendars now depends on getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Nothing in the PR covers another user (or a negative delegation id) being rejected, a successful delete actually removing rows, or expired versus live rows being mapped to cacheUpdatedAt. A regression in the ownership where-clause would ship silently.
